title: KP14 3c blueprint: loading c z~^2 on a cash-flow-level ladder (a pure scale in KP14) whose levels [1.0, 0.38, 0.58] place the types at the fifths of size after the exposure's own effect on value: b = [0.0, 0.35, 0.35], exact compensation, price 2.5
question: On the one 3c blueprint (loading c z~^2 on a scale ladder, both ends exposed), is the true weight non-monotone in the characteristic and the fair gap above 0.02?
notes:
2026-11-10: section 3c on ONE BLUEPRINT across the three models (user: 'small and large firms more exposed than the opposite;
the same pattern in KP; for GS the levered U should also have low and high leverage more risky; all on the same basic blueprint').
Types drawn at birth with equal shares; each type has a position z~_f on a scale ladder (BGN: firm scale type_scale; KP14: the
cash-flow level, a pure scale there; GS21: the coupon drawn from 16 nodes); the loading is c times the square of the standardized
position, b_f = c z~_f^2: zero in the middle, positive at both ends, so the smallest and the largest firms (BGN, KP14) or the
least and the most levered (GS21) carry the exposure. Level-compensated at y = 0 (bv_comp 1 / gs_qcomp 1). Five positions at
-1.41, -0.71, 0, 0.71, 1.41 give z~^2 = 2, 0.5, 0, 0.5, 2 -> b = (0.35, 0.0875, 0, 0.0875, 0.35) at c = 0.175.
KP14: a +0.35 loading raises log size by ~5.0 (40.8 b^2 at 1/(1-alpha) = 6.67, measured on vyu5r), so the levels are set to put the
five types one 0.7-log-size step apart AFTER that: 6.67 log l + 40.8 b^2 = (-1.4, -0.7, 0, 0.7, 1.4).

DESIGN. type_share [0.3333333333333333, 0.3333333333333333, 0.3333333333333333], type_bv [0.0, 0.35, 0.35], type_level [1.0, 0.38, 0.58], gamma_v 2.5, bv_comp 1.0; own tables under prefix vyu3.

PRECOMMITMENT STATUS: precommitted=false; ids filled from the Quest build log by the solve script before any seed runs.

PREDICTION (2026-11-10): true weight non-monotone in the characteristic (both ends alike); fair gap at or above +0.02. FALSIFIED if three seeds have room at or below 10% or ten seeds give a gap below 0.02.
